title: Week 1: Movement opportunity 1: Start, pause and stop
objectives: Apply and explain movement opportunity 1: start, pause and stop using the specified independent and transfer tasks.
entry_evidence: An adult confirms the familiar setting and the learner's usual available comfortable route; use established personal care guidance where applicable.

steps.instruction:
Offer five flexible 30-minute sessions across the week, not one prolonged session or a clinical dose. Each session: 2 minutes check/choose,5 gradual comfortable preparation,12 chosen practice,5 explanation/check and6 flexible rest/transition. Shorten or stop as needed; actual movement time is not the whole allocation. No personal health metrics, recording, required contact or performance ranking. Choose two comfortable available movements and practice responding to an agreed start/pause cue. Practice one rule with adult demonstration on a different sequence. A cue can be text, gesture or sound; do not equate hearing with understanding.
Entry check: ask the learner to demonstrate the stated prerequisite with a fresh example. If missing, teach that skill first; do not treat age or an earlier week number as evidence of readiness.

Adult-approved familiar clear space and stable usual seating/support; no special equipment, competition, biometric device or recording.

objectives: Apply and explain movement opportunity 3: pace and rest using the specified independent and transfer tasks.

safety.safer_alternative: Use an accessible ordinary-paper/model/typed explanation when actual performance is inappropriate; record the changed construct and leave unperformed motor, sensory or measurement outcomes unassessed.
